newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso signs power regulator law.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso signs power regulator law.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed Thursday a bill creating the National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL), a new regulator to oversee the power sector, officials said.

The creation of a new power regulator, with powers to determine tariffs and free of the political pressures that have traditionally dictated policy in the sector, is considered a key step in the ongoing privatization of Brazil's power industry.
A copy of the new law said ANEEL would be responsible for regulating the production, transmission, distribution and sale of power in Brazil.
During an initial 36-month period, however, tariff policy would continue to be dictated the Finance and Mines and Energy Mnistries.

The agency would be linked to the Mines and Energy Ministry with its five-person board being nominated by the president and ratified by the Senate. But a management contract and revenues from a tax on power producers would give ANEEL autonomy.
